newsitem.title: POLAND: Rising rates seen keeping Polish bourse bearish.
newsitem.headline: Rising rates seen keeping Polish bourse bearish.

text.p: The Polish bourse is likely to stay under downward pressure with little upside potential next week as macroeconomic concerns, floods and the run-up to September parliamentary elections combine to dampen buying.

Analysts said macroeconomic concerns -- a rapidly rising money supply which fuelled expectations of higher market interest rates -- have been compounded by the recent flooding that swamped almost two percent of the country.

The government is mulling making available as much as 2.5 billion zlotys ($725 million) in flood-relief loans from the central bank but analysts said Poland's hitherto strong economic growth and falling inflation meant the macroeconomy was sunny enough to prevent big selling.
"I don't see any big sell-off -- you can see that in today's turnover which is a lot less than yesterday's," said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.9 percent this week to 15,056.8 points.
Analysts were divided on the effect of Tuesday's news the Securities Commission had notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices.
Analysts said that though largely prices of parallel-floor firms were suspected, main-market Prochnik's plunge on the news might taint the reputation of the overall market.
"(The allegation) hurts a little--it undermines trust in the whole market as it may not just touch the parallel floor," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.
Tarnowski however said the main market might still have some upside next week as the bourse mood was fickle and selective buying after recent falls could cause gains.
Stomil Olsztyn fell for most of the week after last week's confirmation that the tyremaker suffered a net loss in June due to a recall of two defective tyre types.
Analysts said Budimex should extend its Friday 10-percent loss next week after Thursday's news it had revised down its 1997 pre-tax profit forecast.

Chemiskor whose plunges on the parallel market this week helped the WIRR index significantly underperform the WIG, trades on Monday without the 10-percent price fluctuation limit -- it did not trade after price-fixing for three successive sessions due to excess supply.
